versions.name: RXV2-0.9.455-wizard-logo
versions.notes: The wizard has a face: Malcolm's light-hearted wizard-with-helicopter logo now heads the Wizards hub and the New-helicopter checklist.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.454-restart-to-apply
versions.notes: ESC telemetry verdict (proven live: 40.0C flowing on the Goblin770): the wizard could do it all along - features simply apply at BOOT. Saving features now offers the flight-controller restart on the spot, and Before-you-start is back to its three honest tasks (the Ports-tab task was a wrong diagnosis, withdrawn).

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.453-esc-port-truth
versions.notes: Before-you-start gains task 4 (found on the first real build): ESC telemetry cannot be fully enabled from the phone - the Ports tab must name which UART the ESC's data wire uses. The First-time basics tick now says so too.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.452-tidy-wiring
versions.notes: Wiring page tidied: the brand-new-board card is gone - that story now lives on the Before-you-start page (wizard step 1).

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.451-before-you-start
versions.notes: New 'Before you start' page (Malcolm's wording): the one USB session per new helicopter, as three numbered cards - update the firmware; check the serial port on the Configuration tab matches where the receiver is plugged; enable Telemetry on the Receiver tab then Save & Reboot (bottom right). Wizard step 1 opens it.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.450-computer-session-first
versions.notes: Wizard step 1 is now the one-time computer session, right at the top: turn Telemetry ON and set the serial input to the UART you are using (Save restarts the board); update firmware too while you're there. Everything after is phone-only.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.449-honest-first-contact
versions.notes: First-contact truth (tested live on the Goblin770's Nexus X): a factory-mute flight controller ignores incoming CRSF commands too, so it cannot be woken from the receiver side. The Wiring page now says the honest thing: one one-time computer step (Configurator - enable Telemetry - Save, it restarts) and the phone does everything after.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.448-fc-wake
versions.notes: Wake a brand-new flight controller (Malcolm's first real Nexus X setup): factory boards ship with telemetry OFF and sit silent - undiscoverable. The Wiring page now offers (and has a button for) a one-tap Wake: the receiver blind-writes telemetry ON + save + restart over CRSF (the board listens even when mute). Protected: refused whenever a flight controller is already talking, so it can never touch a configured model.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.447-no-preset-map
versions.notes: Channel order no longer offers a 'standard' preset - it links straight to Transmitter channels, where each channel is chosen (or detected) properly.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.446-help-sync
versions.notes: Help text matches the new Features wording (receiver reference gone there too).

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.445-plain-features
versions.notes: First-time basics: the Features card now simply says 'Tick the functions you plan to use'; the receiver-link row is gone (it goes without saying - and the save still quietly keeps it on).

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.444-imu-first
versions.notes: First-time basics reordered per Malcolm: 'Calibrate the flight controller' (IMU) is now the FIRST card - best done flat on a desk before the board goes in (the helicopter may not sit level), and front-or-back mounting does not affect it (the old 'set mounting first' note was wrong for flat boards). Wizard step 4 renamed to match.
